gates/cell: An LSTM carries two things from step to step: the hidden state, h, and a second memory, the cell state, c.
gates/gates: Three gates control the cell. Each is a sigmoid of z, the old h and the new input joined into one vector, so each is a number between zero and one: a dial for how much.
gates/cand: And a candidate, g, from a tan-aitch, proposes new content between minus one and one.
gates/roles: The forget gate, f, scales the old cell. The input gate, i, scales the candidate before it is added. The output gate, o, scales what the cell shows as h.
update/keep: Here is one unit. The old cell holds two, and the forget gate is zero point three, so the cell keeps zero point six.
update/write: The candidate is zero point five and the input gate zero point eight, so it writes zero point four.
update/add: The new cell adds the two: zero point six plus zero point four, exactly one. In symbols, c t is f t times c t minus one, plus i t times g t.
update/show: Then h is the output gate times the tan-aitch of the cell, h t is o t times the tan-aitch of c t: zero point five times zero point seven six, about zero point three eight.
path/path: Now follow the gradient back along the cell. The new cell is f times the old one, plus new content, so one step back just multiplies by f: partial c t, partial c t minus one, is f t.
path/lstm: No weight matrix and no tan-aitch slope in between. With the forget gate at zero point nine five, twenty steps back still keep about a third of the gradient.
path/rnn: A plain RNN that multiplies by a half at each step keeps one part in a million. The cell's update by addition carries memories, and their gradients, a long way.
